sarah_oncall: Quick broadcast — starting 14:05 UTC we observed elevated tail latency in eu1 hosted inference (p95 ~900ms for a subset of traffic). No spike in 5xx but customer experience degraded. Investigating. Status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2823456789

ops-bot: auto-alert: eu1-serving-pool p95=910ms, inflight=2.3k, queue=430, avg_batch=2.6 -> 14:07:12 UTC

kevin_infra: Looking at node metrics. Early signal: large long-context requests + KV cache eviction spikes leading to kernel fallback on several workers.

josh_research: Kernel fallback observed in logs; fallback path adds CPU per-token. I can push a kernel-preference tweak that avoids slow path on supported instance types. Requires rolling restart of non-dedicated nodes (canary 2 -> roll).

marta_prod: Recommend temporary policy: throttle requests >8000 tokens and route >2048 tokens to gptx-lite fallback. I'll prepare customer note.

sarah_oncall: Implemented temporary token-rate limit for large requests and enabled gptx-lite fallback routing. Paused noncritical eval jobs in eu1.

ops-bot: logs (14:09 UTC): [w-9] KV_EVICT key=ctx-99 size=13MB; [w-9] kernel_fallback slow_path_ms=14.7; [w-14] req token_len=11500 batch=1

kevin_infra: Starting canary rolling restart at 14:12 UTC. Healthcheck 30s/node.

ops-bot: metric update (14:16 UTC): p95 -> 300ms, queue -> 140, inflight -> 1.2k

josh_research: Canary nodes show p95 ~220ms on test traffic. Proceeding with remainder.

marta_prod: Sent proactive messages to customers with >1s responses in last hour and updated status page with mitigations.

sarah_oncall: Service stabilized to normal p95 (~200-260ms) at 14:20 UTC after kernel preference change and temporary rate limits. No customer request drops. Postmortem ticket to follow for KV eviction tuning and smarter kernel-selection policy.

statusbot: Created INC-2026-2823456789 -> https://internal.ops.redwood/INC-2026-2823456789; transitioned to Resolved at 14:22 UTC.
